ai_assessment.method: Full direct English-to-Vietnamese comparison of all 3893 canonical passages and both titles. Separate subagent drafting from the original preceded review. A separate-context assessor (same model family, not shown the drafter’s notes or scores) read every pair first and reported about thirteen major and about seventy minor findings with a pre-revision weighted score of 7.68; the drafter revised the text, re-read the changed passages and the whole target for naturalness, then assigned these final scores bound to the final byte hashes.
ai_assessment.limitations: The same AI system drafted, revised and assessed the work; the separate-context pass is correlated same-model feedback, not independent review or model diversity. No human literary reviewer, native-reader trial or measured reader demand is claimed. Existing Vietnamese translations were not consulted or collated. Scores are subjective and uncalibrated; missed errors may remain. Source clearance is separately recorded and is not granted by this review.

findings.explanation: A name used before Pip learns it; the address was rendered without the name.
A comic ditty was given invented narration; restored to the sung lines only.
A lyric was paraphrased rather than rendered; restored.
The Jew’s cousin was rendered as the master; corrected.
A possessive given to Herbert instead of Pip; corrected.
“Twenty minutes to nine” read as 8:20; corrected to 8:40.
The convicts were made to treat the guard; the English has them treating him; corrected.
The referent of “it” was given to Estella instead of Miss Havisham’s breast; corrected.
Estella’s correction of Pip was reversed; restored.
A pronoun pointed at the dog instead of the gentleman; corrected.
“Public boarding-school” gave Compeyson the wrong class; corrected.
A young lady was called a matron; corrected.
A bay-window was mistranslated; corrected to the architectural sense.
The refrain sentence was inverted; restored.
“Goes out of his way” reversed; corrected.
A pew-opener was taken for a collector; corrected.
Joe’s “harm” pun has no Vietnamese equivalent; the sense is kept and the pun is recorded as lost.
The pronouns of Pip’s reply were reversed; corrected.
“Come on your birthday” was given Miss Havisham’s birthday instead of Pip’s; corrected.
Pip’s address and self-reference to Mrs. Joe were inconsistent with the glossary; corrected.
Pumblechook’s triumph was reversed; restored.
“Nevvy” lost its nephew sense; corrected.
“Tea for Joe” was given as tea for coffee, and “that strength” had no referent; corrected.
The convict’s sarcasm (“worth my while to murder him”) was reversed; corrected.
Jaggers’s cool formal register was turned into a rustic bully’s; corrected.
“A gross or two” of screws was rendered as a dozen; corrected to the scale of the joke.

summary: All 3893 units of the complete novel as printed by Project Gutenberg #1400 (1867 edition), translated directly from the English. The first blind reviews of the four slices scored between 7.7 and 8.7 with about thirteen major findings and about seventy minor ones, mostly referents, speakers, address forms, sense reversals and a few lost wordplays. Each slice was revised in fix rounds, and separate-context blind reviews re-checked every change; the named majors listed here are the ones verified against the English. The final confirmation reviews score slice 1 at 8.9, slice 2 at 8.63, slice 3 at 8.8 and slice 4 at 8.7, with no critical or major finding open. The weakest part, 8.63, sets the score. Two known losses are recorded: Joe’s ‘harm’ pun at unit 3747 and the T-word pun at unit 967 have no Vietnamese equivalent, and the sense is kept. Minor findings are recorded in the review files and do not block release.

title_review.rationale: The title follows the translation’s chosen Vietnamese title, ‘Những Kỳ Vọng Lớn’ (Great Expectations); no other Vietnamese edition was checked.
